# Inline Visuals
**English** · 简体中文
### Charts your agent can draw — and your session can replay.

A plugin for DeepSeek Harness that turns
numbers into pictures **inside the conversation**: 18 kinds

of charts, tables, timelines, gantt,
heatmaps, flows and KPI tiles — plus ML/paper visuals such as

training curves, ROC/PR curves,
confusion matrices, leaderboards and embedding clusters. With styles
, exports and click-to-ask.
## Why you'll like it
- **Figures in the answer, not just the tool log.** The final chart of a turn lands beneath the repl

y.
- **See it, don't read it.** "Three caching strategies, compared" becomes a card you scan in two

seconds.
- **It stays.** The card is stored in the session log — refresh, reopen, branch the session

, it is still there.
- **Ask, don't retype.** Click any data point, get a one-click follow-up prompt

in your composer.
- **Change it by talking.** "Make it horizontal and stacked, with labels." The ag

ent patches the chart
with `edit_visual` instead of redrawing everything.
- **Native and safe.** Fol

lows the host theme (light/dark, English/Chinese). The model sends *data*,
never HTML or JavaScript.
- **Made for ML & papers.** Training curves with log axes, smoothing and error bars; ROC/PR with AU
JSON/CSV, export PNG or SVG.

nline-visuals`, or point Plugin Manager at a local clone

## Try it
Just talk to your agent:
> **"Compare three caching strategies — hit rate, memory and complexity — as a chart."**
> **"Turn that into a horizontal stacked bar, and add value labels."**
> **"Draw our release pipeline as a flow."**
> **"Show last week's traffic as a heatmap."**
## What it can draw

| **Charts** | bar · line · area · pie · doughnut · scatter · radar · waterfall |
| **ML & papers**
| training curves · ROC/PR curves · confusion matrix · histogram · model leaderboard · embedding sca

tter |
| **Everything else** | compare table · timeline · gantt · heatmap · flow · KPI tiles |
Every visual accepts presentation **styles**: horizontal or stacked bars, stepped lines, data labels

,
legends, grids, five palettes, height and density, scatter trend lines, log axes, EMA smoothing an

ids, five palettes, height and density, scatter trend lines, log axes, EMA smoothing and
error bars.
## Built for ML & paper reading
Reading a paper or a training log? Ask for the figure:
> **"Plot train/val loss for 8 epochs on a log scale, smoothed, with error bars."**
> **"Draw the ROC curve from these points and mark AUC."**
> **"Make a confusion matrix for cat/dog/bird from this table."**
> **"Compare these four models on accuracy, F1 and latency — highlight the best."**
> **"Cluster these embeddings by class and show a t-SNE scatter."**
## How it works (in one breath)
The model sends a small, declarative spec → the plugin validates and stores it on the tool result →
your client renders it with the host's theme. Because the data lives in the session log, replays nee

d
no extra model call.
## FAQ
**Do I need to configure anything?** No. Install and ask.
**Where do the cards live?** In the session log (`tool/result.meta`), not in a separate file.
**Does it send my data anywhere?** No. The plugin performs no network calls; the model already sees

my data anywhere?** No. The plugin performs no network calls; the model already sees
what you typed.
**Can I get the numbers out?** Copy as JSON or CSV; charts export as PNG; hand-drawn cards as SVG.
**Which kinds are interactive?** Click-to-ask works on chart kinds (canvas). More surfaces are on th

nds are interactive?** Click-to-ask works on chart kinds (canvas). More surfaces are on the
roadmap.
**Text-only clients?** They receive a compact text summary instead of the card — nothing is lost.
## Under the hood

- 38 tests (`node:test`), CI on every push, tag-driven npm release with provenance.
- ~35 KB host ha

lf, one self-contained browser file (~217 KB, Chart.js inlined, React shared with the host).
- Spec
`version: 3` is stable; v1/v2 specs still render.

Full parameter reference, limits and development notes: **docs/reference.md**.
